name: The "inflammation is the root of all disease" story
name_rule: Attributed, not asserted (briefs/narratives/SYSTEM.md §3): a name is one more repetition of the claim.
former_claim_names: Inflammation Is the Root of All Disease
claim: Chronic low-grade inflammation, driven by modern diet, is the hidden cause of fatigue, pain and most chronic disease — and eating specific 'anti-inflammatory' foods can reverse it.
predictor: Andrew Weil · Mark Hyman (earliest and most-cited carriers in this corpus)
born_note: Model estimate: mid-2000s diet-book framing of inflammation as the universal disease driver (pending audit). This corpus reaches back to 2019; the root-cause claim is stated in its earliest dated claims (Andrew Weil, 2021).

mutations.mechanism: chronic inflammation as the shared root of disease — food lists and turmeric as the cure
seed oils named as the main villain
the gut microbiome as the route — fibre and fermented food as the lever
the seed-oil backlash — human-trial rebuttals outnumber the alarms; sugar, insulin and ultra-processed food take the blame

explanations.layman: A popular health idea says hidden 'inflammation' inside your body is behind tiredness, aches and most illness — and that eating the right foods can calm it down. Doctors and creators publish endless food lists promising more energy and less pain. Some of it rests on real science; much of it is simplified into shopping lists that sell books, supplements and courses.
explanations.intermediate: The narrative links chronic low-grade inflammation to obesity, heart disease, depression and pain, then proposes dietary correction: polyphenols, omega-3s, fibre, fewer ultra-processed foods. Camps: mainstream nutrition science (inflammation matters but is one factor among many, effects modest) versus wellness-media maximalism (inflammation is THE cause, food is the cure). The listicle format is the narrative's dominant delivery vehicle.
explanations.expert: Lifecycle: mature and heavily commercialised. Clocks are weak — claims are chronic-condition framed, so rarely falsified in public. Falsifiers: RCTs showing biomarker changes (CRP, IL-6) without hard-outcome benefit; heterogeneity of dietary inflammatory indices. Incentives: cookbooks, supplement affiliates, clinic funnels. Watch for mutation into gut-microbiome and 'metabolic health' framings, which absorb the same audience.

mutations_basis: Dated to the first year a framing reached at least 3 videos and 20% of that year's corpus (transcript review, 2026-09-15). The corpus favours recent uploads, so early years are thin.

trigger.title: 10 anti-inflammatory foods for more energy, less pain and better health
trigger.note: The pasted video that founded this narrative on the live engine (twice — the duplicate was merged).
